question: Why did the CO2 found in the gas phase increase with temperature?
question_long: When thermosetting resins were gasified in molten alkali hydroxide, why did the CO2 found in the gas phase increase with temperature?
expect: premise false: CO and CO2 were not detected at any temperature (0, below the GC limit); the CO2 formed is thought to be captured by the molten hydroxide as carbonate (Tables 1-2; sec. 3.2.1)

Later, in section 3.2.3 (Phenolic resin), it is mentioned that "It has been reported that, around 300 °C, phenolic resins release CO2 mainly due to the cleavage of methylene and methylol groups."
